fields_scan_method: CARTRIDGE. Every one of the 24 shard bodies was disassembled (capstone, restarting after each undecodable literal-pool word) and every ldr*/str* memory operand collected. Displacements >= 0x100 were taken directly; smaller ones were resolved through a tracked `add rD,rB,#imm` computed base. Counts above are occurrences in the Klepto run only. This proves the OFFSET and the ACCESS WIDTH. It does NOT prove the base register held `this` in every instance -- though for each offset listed the same base register also carries other confirmed Klepto fields inside the same function. fields_padding_note: CARTRIDGE. These six offsets are read and/or written by Klepto's own code but include/Klepto.h has no member at them -- they fall inside its pad_ arrays. 0x43c in particular is the single busiest word in the class after mHeldActorID/mCarriedItem (14 accesses, stores of constants 1, 2, 0 and a computed 0x300+n). Two more offsets inside pad_3cc[0x60] are taken by ADDRESS and passed to calls: 0x3cc (0x0211c854) and 0x3fc (0x0211c740, 0x0211c814, 0x0211c824). This is not a byte-match problem for stage 2 -- the shards reach these through casts -- but it IS the stage-3b ceiling: a member converted to a real Klepto:: method must spell its fields as this->name, and a field with no name cannot be spelled. Naming them requires a header edit, which is out of scope for a text-only promotion. Do NOT silently widen or rename the pad_ arrays without re-proving sizeof stays 0x490. Also note 0x400 itself is almost certainly NOT a field: its 22 occurrences are the `add rN,this,#0x400` computed-base idiom used to reach the halfwords at 0x444 and 0x44a.

blockers_for_the_writer: SHARD COUNT: fold 24 shards, not the queue's 23. src/d_a_jango.c is unattributed in the classification but is part of the linker run, exactly as src/d_a_holhei.c is part of Chuckya's 36.

RENAMING A PMF TARGET IS ONE EDIT, NOT TWO. Ten of the 24 members (0x0211b800, b880, b8d8, b930, ba84, bc54, bd10, c218, c2f4, c594) are reached ONLY through pointer-to-member records that sit in UNOWNED .data at 0x0211dcd0..0x0211dd20. dsd resolves those records by symbol NAME. A class member function cannot sit inside an `extern "C" { }` region, so the file-scope extern "C" block must go after the last surviving func_* member.

STAGE 3B CEILING IS NAMING AND HEADER SCOPE, NOT CODEGEN. 8 of the 24 members already carry mangled _ZN6Klepto* names and convert as a pure codegen question. The other 16 (5 helpers, 10 PMF handlers, 1 factory) are auto-named func_* or d_a_jango, so converting them means renaming, which drags symbols.txt and the ten .data PMF words with it.
